desc: Juno, in a polar orbit around Jupiter since 2016, mapping its gravity, magnetic field and deep atmosphere.
Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, imaging Mars at 30 cm resolution since 2006.
James Webb Space Telescope, launched December 2021, observing in the infrared from a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L2 point 1.5 million km from Earth.
SOHO, the Solar and Heliospheric Observatory, watching the Sun from the L1 point since 1996.
BepiColombo, joint ESA/JAXA mission to Mercury, launched 2018, due to enter orbit in late 2026.
Europa Clipper, launched October 2024, en route to Jupiter's ocean moon Europa, arriving in 2030.
Launched 1972, the first spacecraft to cross the asteroid belt and fly past Jupiter. Contact was lost in 2003; it coasts toward Aldebaran.
STEREO-A, watching the Sun from a heliocentric orbit ahead of Earth since 2006.
Launched 1973. First spacecraft to fly past Saturn (1979). Contact was lost in 1995.
Psyche, launched 2023, travelling to the metal-rich asteroid 16 Psyche, arriving in 2029.
JUICE, ESA's Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer, launched 2023, arriving at Jupiter in 2031.
Launched 1977. Flew past Jupiter and Saturn, then crossed the heliopause into interstellar space in 2012. The most distant human-made object, still transmitting with a 22-watt radio.
Launched 1977. The only spacecraft to visit all four giant planets; entered interstellar space in 2018.
Hayabusa2, returned samples of asteroid Ryugu in 2020 and is on an extended mission to asteroid 1998 KY26.
Lucy, launched 2021, on a 12-year tour of eight Trojan asteroids that share Jupiter's orbit.
Parker Solar Probe, launched 2018. Repeatedly dives through the Sun's corona, reaching within 6.1 million km of the surface at 690,000 km/h, the fastest object ever built.
Launched 2006. Flew past Pluto in July 2015 and the Kuiper Belt object Arrokoth in 2019, now heading out of the Solar System.
